doctrine: A menu of starting points, never a fence. Combine, bend or ignore any entry, or invent a new form (invented: {name, why}); gates judge the outcome (budget, legibility, honesty), never whether a form is listed here.

selection.step1: score every behaviour: distinct text signals matched (capped) + weights of structural features present; the DOMINANT behaviour wins, the runner-up is recorded
selection.step2: score the suggested layout types of the dominant (and runner-up) behaviour: suggestion rank + fit weights of features present + type-level text signals - a penalty per unmet requirement (requirements are not penalised when no items are given: unknown is not absent)

tie_breakers.rule: items carry 3 or more attributes, there are no relations and no branches, and the dominant behaviour is not one where the shape of the values is the message -> table
the chosen type is marked table_equivalent and a 3-column table holds the same content (no relations, no branches, at most 2 attributes per item, at most 12 items) -> table
when two behaviours both fit, the higher score is the layout grammar; the runner-up may add at most one primitive, otherwise split into two figures

faithful_exemption.why: a zoned faithful redraw may exceed the overview budget; above 24 nodes, split

low.keep: half the nodes (rounded up), most important first

medium.keep: all nodes up to the type's node budget; the least connected beyond it are cut

high.keep: every node; the budget gate proposes a split if over

detail_levels.rank: importance (if given), then degree, then input order
detail_levels.rule: the detail dial changes HOW MANY nodes are drawn, never what they are called

audience_levels.plain: plain words: the item's `plain` label, else its label with code punctuation removed
audience_levels.mixed: plain name with the exact field name as a sublabel
audience_levels.rule: the audience dial changes WHAT nodes are called, never how many are drawn

features.no_relations: the description has no relations between items
features.fan_in: some item receives 3 or more relations (many sources, one sink)
features.branching: an item has 2 or more outgoing relations carrying conditions, or an item is a decision
features.linear_chain: the relations form one unbranched path through 3 or more items
features.tree_shaped: one root, every other item has exactly one parent, no cycle, and something branches
features.multi_parent: some item has 2 or more incoming relations (a shared dependency)
features.has_cycle: following the relations can return to an item already visited
features.item_quantities: 2 or more items carry a numeric value
features.signed_values: item values include both increases and decreases
features.time_axis: the content is ordered in time (has_time_axis, or items/relations carry times)
features.messages: 2 or more relations are messages (call, request, response, event...)
features.actors: 2 or more items are actors or participants
features.zones: items sit in 2 or more named zones
features.zone_crossing: a relation joins items in different zones
features.layered_items: 3 or more items carry a layer or level
features.attributes3: items carry 3 or more attributes each (on average)
features.two_numeric_axes: 3 or more items, each with 2 or 3 numeric attributes
features.states: 3 or more items are states, or 2 or more relations are transitions
features.containment: 2 or more relations mean contains / part of / child of
features.depends: 2 or more relations mean depends on / requires / imports
features.two_traces: exactly two traces (two policies or inputs) are compared
features.owners: 2 or more items are people, teams, roles or owners
features.has_relations: the description has relations between items

behaviours.label: where things are in a space
loose input becomes a structured record
build vs buy on an evolution axis

types.name: Architecture
use_when: components and the connections between them in one snapshot
grouping by tier or trust zone (zones variant)

not_this.when: the point is which host, zone or replica runs what
the order of messages over time matters
who does what at each step of a pipeline

types.name: Trust-boundary map
use_when: which routes cross a trust boundary and which are blocked
permitted versus forbidden ingress or deploy paths

not_this.when: there is no permitted/forbidden distinction, only topology
the controls themselves, grouped by where they are enforced

types.name: Architecture delta
use_when: structural change between two topology snapshots, with a ledger of what changed

not_this.when: only attributes change, the topology does not
the order of the migration phases matters

types.name: Current-state landscape
use_when: today's tools and hand-offs grouped by phase or department, with pain points flagged

not_this.when: you also have the target picture
there are no pain points to show, just a neutral snapshot

types.name: Hub and spoke
use_when: what plugs into a central system, what it exposes, and over which interface

not_this.when: peer components with no single hub

types.name: Data flow
use_when: how data or work moves through a pipeline: sources converging, typed payloads, who touches it
fan-in into a constrained point

not_this.when: business hand-offs where the payload type does not matter
the amounts on each path are the story
the steps, not the sources, dominate

types.name: Queue / bottleneck
use_when: many arrivals compete for one finite service point; queue depth, capacity and wait are the story

not_this.when: there is no capacity limit, only convergence

types.name: Process
use_when: sequential steps with owners, inputs and outputs per step
a stage framework that repeats the same slots per stage

not_this.when: payloads and tools do not matter, only who hands off to whom
front-stage versus back-stage is the point

types.name: Swimlane
use_when: a cross-functional process with hand-offs between named owners

not_this.when: what the customer sees versus what stays hidden
the question is who owns what, not the flow
each step's payload must be legible

types.name: Flowchart
use_when: decision logic with branches and outcomes
algorithms, triage and eligibility rules

not_this.when: branches never re-join and every path ends in its own outcome

types.name: Decision tree
use_when: a cascade of questions where each answer narrows to a distinct outcome and paths never re-merge

not_this.when: each outcome is one row of conditions with no order between questions

types.name: Paired policy traces
use_when: two similar inputs reach different outcomes; rule-by-rule pass / fail / skipped / not reached and the first divergence

not_this.when: there is one decision path and nothing to compare
the order of the rules does not matter

types.name: Sequence
use_when: time-ordered messages between actors: request/response, protocol exchanges, call traces

not_this.when: one subject's states, not messages between actors
events on a calendar with no actors

types.name: State machine
use_when: finite states, transitions and guards: order status, connection lifecycle, job status

not_this.when: messages between actors carry the story
one subject's happy path with separate wait and terminal bands

types.name: Lifecycle phase map
use_when: one subject moves through 4-5 phases while waits, retries, cancellation and terminal outcomes matter as much as the happy path

not_this.when: dense guards and events matter more than the subject's progress

types.name: Entity-relationship
use_when: entities and cardinality in a conceptual or domain model

not_this.when: physical tables, SQL types and column-level keys

types.name: Database schema
use_when: real tables, types, constraints and column-to-column foreign keys

not_this.when: the conversation is about what an entity is, not how it is stored

types.name: Class diagram
use_when: classes with operations, inheritance and composition

not_this.when: there are no operations and no inheritance

types.name: Dependency graph
use_when: what depends on what, with shared dependencies (several parents) or a cycle a tree cannot show

not_this.when: every node has one parent and nothing points back
too many nodes and edges for a readable graph

types.name: Dependency structure matrix
use_when: dense dependencies among many modules, where a graph would be a hairball

not_this.when: 9 nodes or fewer: a ranked graph reads faster
values, not dependencies, fill the cells

types.name: Tree
use_when: parent-to-child hierarchy, taxonomy, decomposition into addressable blocks

not_this.when: a node has several parents or there is a cycle
the nodes are people, teams or owners
containment or scope is the point, not the branching

types.name: Org chart / responsibility map
use_when: who owns what: teams, roles, escalation and routing

not_this.when: the process, not the ownership, is the question

types.name: Nested containment
use_when: containment or scope: outer is broader, inner is more specific (blast radius, scope levels)

not_this.when: siblings must sit side by side

types.name: Mind map
use_when: a central idea with loosely related branches; exploration rather than strict levels

types.name: Layer stack
use_when: stacked abstraction levels or layered controls in a fixed order

not_this.when: the physical parts of one object

types.name: Control catalog
use_when: controls grouped by where they are enforced, with who enforces them and when

not_this.when: one control per layer: a plain stack
who may do what is the comparison

types.name: Compensating layers
use_when: each defence covers a gap the previous one left, and residual risk narrows through the stack

not_this.when: no risk propagates between the layers

types.name: Exploded view
use_when: the physical parts of one object pulled apart along one axis

not_this.when: nothing has a footprint or a thickness

types.name: Floor / site plan
use_when: rooms or buildings on one floor or site, seen from above

not_this.when: a list of rooms and capacities

types.name: Venn / set overlap
use_when: overlap between 2-3 sets where the intersection is the point

not_this.when: 4 or more sets: use a matrix
one set fully contains the other

types.name: Pyramid
use_when: a ranked hierarchy: the narrow apex is rarest or most valuable

types.name: Funnel
use_when: an ordered drop-off through the stages of one population

types.name: Bar chart
use_when: one value compared across categories

not_this.when: two values per category and the gap between them
the categories are time and the trend matters
the values are parts of one whole

types.name: Dumbbell
use_when: two values per category where the gap is the message: before/after, target/actual

not_this.when: the steps between the two totals matter
the rank change across the two states matters

types.name: Waterfall
use_when: a start total bridged to an end total by signed contributions

types.name: Treemap
use_when: part of a whole where the relative sizes are the story

not_this.when: exact values matter more than proportion
you must trace parent to child

types.name: Marimekko
use_when: a two-level share: column width is the category's share, segment height the series' share

not_this.when: the cells carry rates, not shares

types.name: Heatmap
use_when: a row x column grid where one combination stands out

not_this.when: fewer than 3 rows: a table says it with less ink

types.name: Access matrix
use_when: who can do what: roles x resources with a permission in each cell

not_this.when: who talks to what over which interface

types.name: Line chart
use_when: continuous change over time: the direction and rate of change

types.name: Slopegraph
use_when: exactly two states and several series, read as slope and rank change

not_this.when: the gap matters, not the rank

types.name: Bump chart
use_when: rank movement across 3-6 snapshots

types.name: Ridgeline
use_when: one distribution per series, stacked on one shared scale

types.name: Streamgraph
use_when: a total and its composition changing across many periods

not_this.when: the series are independent, not parts of a total

types.name: Timeline
use_when: dated events and milestones, spaced honestly in time

types.name: Gantt chart
use_when: tasks with start and end dates grouped by phase: overlap and parallel tracks

types.name: Scatter plot
use_when: two continuous variables: correlation, clusters, outliers

not_this.when: the four regions, not the exact positions, are the message
one variable, one dot per item

types.name: Bubble chart
use_when: two variables plus a third shown as area

not_this.when: the third value does not change the story

types.name: Beeswarm
use_when: one variable, one dot per item, where the shape of the crowd is the story

types.name: Histogram
use_when: the distribution of one variable in bins

types.name: Box plot
use_when: distributions of a few groups compared by median, spread and outliers

not_this.when: the full shape of each distribution matters

types.name: Radar
use_when: 3-5 entities scored on 3-5 quantitative criteria, compared by shape

not_this.when: two entities, or the exact values matter

types.name: Polar chart
use_when: one series across 4-8 categories whose circular order means something (hours, months)

types.name: Quadrant (2x2)
use_when: two-axis positioning or prioritisation: impact x effort, 2x2 trade-offs

not_this.when: four named futures, not positioned items

types.name: Scenario matrix
use_when: four named scenarios across two independent drivers

not_this.when: items are positioned inside the cells

types.name: Loop / flywheel
use_when: a reinforcing cycle where each pass writes back to a shared hub

not_this.when: the path ends or branches to an outcome

types.name: Cycle
use_when: a repeating sequence of steps that returns to the start, with no hub

types.name: Causal loop
use_when: variables that push each other up or down, with reinforcing and balancing loops

types.name: Sankey
use_when: a quantity splitting and merging across up to 3 stages, band width = amount

not_this.when: a single narrowing quantity with no splits

types.name: Fishbone (cause and effect)
use_when: the causes of one observed effect, grouped by category

types.name: Value-chain evolution map
use_when: components of a value chain placed by how evolved they are: what to build, buy, or expect to move

types.name: Kanban board
use_when: a snapshot of work by state, with WIP limits and blocked items

not_this.when: the flow between states needs arrows

types.name: Journey map
use_when: what one person does across the stages of an experience and how it feels

not_this.when: there is no sentiment to name

types.name: Service blueprint
use_when: customer actions versus what the service hides, across stages, with a line of visibility

types.name: Deployment
use_when: where software runs: zones, hosts, replicas and versions

not_this.when: there is no placement decision, only logical topology

types.name: Story map
use_when: a narrative backbone sliced into releases, with the cut line

types.name: Loose input to structured record
use_when: a conversation or notes become a structured record, with provenance from statement to field

types.name: Tier ladder
use_when: the same artefact promoted through quality tiers, each with its own contents and access

types.name: Network
use_when: many-to-many links with no hierarchy or rank: who is connected to whom

not_this.when: the edges have direction and rank

types.name: Small multiples
use_when: the same small chart repeated per category so shapes can be compared

not_this.when: 5 series or fewer fit on one chart

types.name: Table
use_when: items x attributes where no relation, branch or shape carries meaning: a 3-column table says the same

not_this.when: 3-5 entities whose score shapes must be compared at a glance
one combination must stand out in a large grid
